200: Banya the Explosive Delivery Man by Kim Young-Oh (Dark Horse) is a fantasy action manhwa about a courier who never fails a job. In a war-torn world full of monsters and armies, Banya works for a delivery service that will carry anything anywhere, no matter the danger. He is fearless, cocky, and very hard to stop. It is a fast, hard-hitting adventure for readers who like brawls, journeys, and a hero with a big grin.
202: Sanda by Paru Itagaki (Titan) is a quirky action comedy with a holiday twist. In a future Japan where children are rare and Christmas has been all but forgotten, middle schooler Kazushige Sanda learns he can transform into Santa Claus. His classmate Shiori Fuyumura discovers his secret and demands his help finding her missing best friend. It is strange, funny, and surprisingly heartfelt, a good pick for fans of Beastars looking for something wilder.
205: The Faraway Paladin by Kanata Yanagino (J-Novel Club) is a gentle, thoughtful fantasy light novel. After a wasted life, a man is reborn as Will, a boy raised in a ruined city by three undead guardians: the skeleton warrior Blood, the mummy priestess Mary, and the ghost sorcerer Gus. As he grows, he begins to wonder why they live there and what lies beyond. It suits readers who like warm found family, careful worldbuilding, and a hero who wants to live well this time.
206: The Bocchi the Rock! Comic Anthology by various artists (Yen Press) is a collection of short comedy stories set in the world of Bocchi the Rock! Hitori "Bocchi" Gotoh is a painfully shy girl who plays guitar brilliantly alone in her room, until she is pulled into the scrappy Kessoku Band. Here, a range of artists put their own spin on Bocchi and her bandmates, making it a light, fun extra for fans who want more of the band's daily chaos.
215: D.N.Angel by Yukiru Sugisaki (Yen Press) is a shojo romantic comedy with a gentleman-thief twist. On his fourteenth birthday, mild-mannered Daisuke Niwa plans to confess to his crush, Risa Harada. Instead he learns his family's secret: whenever he thinks of the girl he loves, he transforms into the legendary phantom thief Dark. It mixes heists, magic, and teenage heartache, a fun pick for fans of classic 2000s shojo.
224: I Got Married to the Girl I Hate Most in Class by Seiju Amano (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy light novel. High schooler Saito Hojo and his classmate Akane Sakuramori can't stand each other, so they are horrified when their grandparents arrange for them to marry. Now they share a house, and they have to keep the marriage secret at school. It is a sweet, bickering slow-burn for readers who enjoy rivals-to-lovers stories.
230: The Three-Body Problem by Cixin Liu, adapted by XuDong Cai (Yen Press), is a sci-fi drama manhua based on the award-winning novel. Nanomaterials researcher Wang Miao is pulled into a police investigation after a wave of scientists take their own lives. His search leads him to a strange virtual reality game and a secret reaching back to China's Cultural Revolution. It is a thoughtful, big-idea story for readers who enjoy hard science fiction and slow-building mysteries.
238: Shugo Chara! by Peach-Pit (Kodansha) is a magical-girl comedy about finding your true self. At school, Amu Hinamori has a cool, rebellious image that everyone admires, but inside she is shy and unsure of herself. One night she wishes she could be reborn as the person she wants to be, and in the morning she finds three eggs in her bed. It is bright, funny, and heartfelt, a great fit for younger readers and fans of classic shojo.
242: A Misanthrope Teaches a Class for Demi-Humans by Kurusu Natsume, with art by Atsu Benino (Yen Press), is a gentle school comedy. Hitoma Kirihara is a young teacher who would rather avoid people entirely. Then he is assigned to a high school for demi-human girls, where his students include an elf, a mermaid, and other beings who all have their own worries. It is a warm, low-stakes slice of life about a grump slowly learning to care.
243: Alya Sometimes Hides Her Feelings in Russian by Sunsunsun, with art by Saho Tenamachi (Yen Press), is a sweet romantic comedy. Alisa Mikhailovna Kujou, the aloof top student at her school, treats her lazy seatmate Masachika Kuze with cool disdain, though she sometimes mutters affectionate things to him in Russian, sure he can't understand. What she doesn't know is that Masachika understands every word. It is a playful, teasing romance for fans of will-they-won't-they stories.
244: Chronicles of an Aristocrat Reborn in Another World (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure light novel about building a team. A man is reborn as Ars Louvent, the son of a minor noble in a land on the edge of war, with one special skill: Appraisal, which reveals the hidden talents of anyone he meets. Ars sets out to find gifted people and bring them to his side. It suits readers who enjoy strategy, recruiting, and steady kingdom building.
248: The High School Life of a Fudanshi by Atami Michinoku (Seven Seas) is a light school comedy. Ryo Sakaguchi is an ordinary high school boy with a passion that surprises everyone: he is a fudanshi, a male fan of boys' love manga, and he isn't shy about it. The story follows Ryo and his friends through fan conventions, bookstore runs, and everyday mix-ups. It is a breezy, good-natured read for anyone who has ever loved a fandom.
251: Nana by Ai Yazawa (Viz Media) is a josei drama about friendship, music, and growing up. Two twenty-year-old women, both named Nana, meet by chance on a train to Tokyo and later end up sharing an apartment. Nana Komatsu is a romantic chasing love, while Nana Osaki is a punk singer chasing a music career, and their friendship becomes the heart of the story. It is honest, stylish, and emotional, a favorite for readers who like character-driven stories about adult life.
259: Mechanical Marie by Aki Akimoto (Yen Press) is a shojo romantic comedy with a secret at its center. Arthur, the young heir of a powerful family, distrusts people and will only let robots near him. So Marie, a plain young woman, takes a job as his personal maid by pretending to be a robot, and keeping up the act only gets harder as Arthur starts to open up to her. It is a funny, sweet read for fans of disguise and slow-burn romance.
274: Franken Fran by Katsuhisa Kigitsu (Seven Seas) is a darkly funny horror manga. Fran Madaraki is a cheerful girl stitched together by the brilliant surgeon Dr. Madaraki, and while he travels, she runs his lab and takes in anyone who comes to her for help. Fran always means well, but her bizarre surgical fixes rarely turn out the way anyone expects. It is gory, gross, and clever, best for mature readers who like their horror with a grin.
275: Orb: On the Movements of the Earth by Uoto (Seven Seas) is a historical drama about the search for truth. In fifteenth-century Europe, the church teaches that the Earth is the center of the universe, and questioning it is heresy. Rafal, a gifted boy headed for a safe career in theology, meets a scholar who is secretly studying the heavens, and that meeting changes his life. It is a gripping, thoughtful story for readers who enjoy ideas, history, and moral stakes.
277: .hack//Legend of the Twilight by Rei Izumi (Tokyopop) is a fantasy adventure set inside a video game. Twins Shugo and Rena win a contest that gives them special characters in The World, a huge online role-playing game, modeled on the legendary players Kite and BlackRose. Once they log in, they find the game hiding strange glitches and dangers. It is a fun, light adventure for gamers and fans of the .hack franchise.
279: Star Wars: Lost Stars by Claudia Gray (Yen Press) is a sci-fi romance adapted from her novel. Thane Kyrell and Ciena Ree grow up on the remote planet Jelucan, sharing a dream of flying for the Empire. They become close friends at the Imperial Academy, but as the galaxy goes to war, they end up on opposite sides. It is a moving story about loyalty and love, a great fit for Star Wars fans who want something more personal.
285: Missing by Gakuto Coda (Tokyopop) is a supernatural mystery based on the Japanese light novels. Kyoichi Utsume is a quiet, sharp-tongued member of his school's literature club, and when he vanishes after meeting a mysterious girl, his friends in the club refuse to give up. Their search draws them into old legends about people who are spirited away. It is eerie and moody, a good pick for readers who like ghost stories and urban legends.
286: Suzume by Makoto Shinkai (Kodansha) is a fantasy adventure adapted from his animated film. Suzume Iwato is a high school girl in a quiet town in Kyushu, and one morning she meets a young man looking for a door. Her curiosity leads her to open something that should have stayed shut, and soon she is traveling across Japan to close doors that bring disaster. It is beautiful, heartfelt, and full of road-trip charm, a great fit for fans of the film.
290: Tales of Berseria by Nobu Aonagi (Kodansha) is a dark fantasy action manga based on the video game. Velvet Crowe lives a quiet life in a small village with her younger brother, until one terrible night shatters everything. She is left with a burning need for revenge against a man she once trusted, and her quest sets her against the whole world. It is intense and emotional, a good pick for fans of the Tales series and antihero stories.
294: Ms. Koizumi Loves Ramen Noodles by Naru Narumi (Dark Horse) is a cozy comedy about food. Yu Osawa is fascinated by her new classmate Koizumi, a beautiful, quiet girl who ignores almost everyone, and soon discovers her one great love: ramen. Whatever the weather, Koizumi is out hunting down the best bowls in town, and Yu is determined to tag along. It is light, funny, and mouthwatering, a fun read for foodies and slice-of-life fans.
298: Golgo 13 by Takao Saito (Viz Media) is a classic seinen thriller about a man who never misses. Duke Togo, known as Golgo 13, is a silent, mysterious professional sniper hired by governments, criminals, and corporations around the world. Each story drops him into a new mission tied to real-world politics and intrigue. It is gritty, tense, and episodic, best for mature readers who enjoy spy fiction and Cold War-era action.
299: Goodbye, My Rose Garden by Dr. Pepperco (Seven Seas) is a historical romance set in early 1900s England. Hanako Kitagawa travels from Japan to London hoping to meet the author of a novel she adores, and instead becomes a maid to Alice Holiday, a young noblewoman with a lovely rose garden. Then Alice makes a shocking request: she asks Hanako to kill her. It is a quiet, tender yuri drama for readers who like period settings and emotional depth.
302: Grimgar of Fantasy and Ash by Ao Jyumonji (Yen Press) is a grounded fantasy adventure based on the light novels. Haruhiro wakes up in a strange world with no memory of how he got there, and with a handful of other lost people, he becomes a volunteer soldier who must form a party just to survive. There are no cheat skills here, only hard work, fear, and friendship. It suits readers who like realistic, character-focused fantasy.
305: Hana and Hina After School by Milk Morinaga (Seven Seas) is a sweet yuri slice of life. Hana Sato quietly loves cute things and works part-time at a shop full of plushies and accessories. One day a new coworker arrives, Hina, a cool, tomboyish girl from another class who loves cute things too, and the two slowly grow closer. It is soft, gentle, and charming, perfect for fans of tender romance.
306: Attack on Titan: No Regrets by Gun Snark, with art by Hikaru Suruga (Kodansha), is an action drama prequel to Attack on Titan. Before he was humanity's strongest soldier, Levi was a thug living in the lawless Underground with his friends Isabel and Farlan. When Erwin Smith of the Survey Corps offers them a way out, they join his ranks with their own hidden plans. It is a gripping backstory for fans of Levi and the Survey Corps.
308: Ayashimon by Yuji Kaku (Viz Media) is a shonen action comedy from the creator of Hell's Paradise. Maruo Urabe dreams of becoming a chivalrous yakuza like the heroes of old gangster movies, but real gangsters aren't what he hoped. Then he meets Urara, a supernatural girl who is an ayashimon, a kind of monster, and together they set out to build a new kind of gang. It is loud, funny, and full of fights.
312: Bakemonogatari by NisiOisin (Vertical) is a supernatural mystery light novel. High schooler Koyomi Araragi catches his classmate Hitagi Senjougahara when she falls down a staircase and discovers she weighs almost nothing. She has been touched by an oddity, a strange supernatural being, and Koyomi, who has his own history with them, offers to help her and others like her. It is witty, wordy, and offbeat, a great fit for fans of the anime and sharp dialogue.
322: Beyblade by Takao Aoki (Viz Media) is a kids action manga about battling spinning tops. Tyson Granger is a boy who lives for Beyblade, a sport where players launch tops into a stadium to knock each other out. With his powerful Beyblade, Dragoon, he takes on rivals and sets out to become the best. It is fast, energetic, and full of friendly rivalry, a great pick for young readers and fans of the anime.
326: The Rising of the Shield Hero by Aneko Yusagi, with art by Aiya Kyu (One Peace Books), is a fantasy action manga about a hero nobody wants. College student Naofumi Iwatani is summoned to another world as the Shield Hero, one of four legendary heroes, but unlike the others he can't attack. Soon after arriving he is betrayed and falsely accused, and bitter and alone, he has to find his own way to fight. It suits readers who like underdog stories and slow redemption arcs.
332: I Shall Survive Using Potions! by FUNA (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy comedy light novel. After an unexpected death, Kaoru Nagase is sent to a new world by a god who feels he owes her one, with a single power: she can create any potion she can imagine. Kaoru decides to use it to live a quiet, safe life, though things rarely stay quiet. It is light, clever fun for readers who like isekai with a resourceful heroine.
338: Blue Giant by Shinichi Ishizuka (Seven Seas) is a coming-of-age drama about jazz. Dai Miyamoto is a high school basketball player in Sendai until he hears jazz and falls in love with it. He teaches himself the tenor saxophone, practicing alone by the river every day, rain or shine, with the dream of becoming the greatest jazz player in the world. It is passionate and moving, and it makes music leap off the page, even for readers who don't know jazz.
346: Penguindrum by Kunihiko Ikuhara (Seven Seas) is a strange, emotional drama adapted from the anime. Brothers Kanba and Shoma Takakura live with their beloved little sister, Himari, who is seriously ill. When she collapses, a penguin-shaped hat brings her back to life, but the spirit inside it demands that the brothers find the mysterious Penguindrum. It is surreal and full of symbolism, a good pick for readers who love unusual storytelling.
347: The Usagi Yojimbo Saga by Stan Sakai (Dark Horse) is a samurai adventure series. Miyamoto Usagi is a rabbit ronin who wanders a feudal Japan of animal people after the death of his lord. Along the way he protects the helpless, faces bandits and rival warriors, and meets friends old and new. Blending action, humor, and real Japanese history and folklore, it is a timeless pick for readers of all ages.
356: Captain Harlock by Leiji Matsumoto (Seven Seas) is a classic space opera. In the distant future, humanity has grown lazy and comfortable, ignoring the dangers around it. Only Captain Harlock, a scarred space pirate, and the crew of his ship, the Arcadia, are willing to fight when the alien Mazone begin their invasion of Earth. It is moody, romantic, and adventurous, a treat for fans of retro sci-fi and the Leiji Matsumoto universe.
359: Time Stranger Kyoko by Arina Tanemura (Viz Media) is a sci-fi shojo comedy. In the year 3000, Kyoko is the princess of Earth, though she would rather be an ordinary teenage girl. To become queen, she must find twelve magical stones to awaken her twin sister, Chitose, who has been asleep since birth, and she sets off with her friends and a mysterious young man. It is cute, sparkly, and fun, a great fit for fans of Tanemura's other work.
365: Pompo the Cinephile by Shogo Sugitani (Seven Seas) is a comedy drama about making movies. In Nyallywood, Pompo is a young girl who also happens to be a brilliant film producer, and her quiet assistant Gene has spent his whole life watching movies and dreaming of directing. When Pompo hands him the chance to direct her newest script, he has to prove what he can do. It is warm and funny, a love letter to film for anyone who loves stories.
367: Clamp School Detectives by CLAMP (Tokyopop) is a shojo comedy mystery. Nokoru Imonoyama is the charming student council president of the enormous Clamp School, and with his friends Suoh and Akira, he has sworn to help any woman in trouble. Together the three boys take on cases large and small, from lost items to real crimes. It is cheerful and lighthearted, a fun pick for fans of CLAMP's lighter work.
372: Princess Ai by Courtney Love and D.J. Milky (Tokyopop) is a music-driven fantasy romance. Ai, a princess from the magical land of Ai-Land, wakes up in modern Tokyo with no memory of who she is. With a beautiful voice and a mysterious heart-shaped mark, she soon finds herself singing her way toward fame, while romance and danger follow her as her past catches up. It is a glossy, stylish story for fans of 2000s pop culture.
373: Prophecy by Tetsuya Tsutsui (Vertical) is a tense seinen thriller. A figure wearing a newspaper over his face starts posting videos online that predict crimes against people who have wronged others, and then the predictions start coming true. Erika Yoshino of the police cybercrime unit leads the hunt for this "Paperboy" and the people behind him. It is fast and gripping, a good pick for readers who enjoy crime stories about the internet age.
375: Puella Magi Madoka Magica by Magica Quartet, with art by Hanokage (Yen Press), is a dark fantasy adapted from the anime. Madoka Kaname is a kind, ordinary middle schooler until a cute creature named Kyubey offers her a deal: make a contract with him and become a magical girl, and he will grant any wish. A mysterious transfer student warns her not to accept. It takes the magical-girl genre in a darker direction, best for readers who enjoy emotional twists.
376: Tokyo These Days by Taiyo Matsumoto (Viz Media) is a quiet drama about the manga world. Shiozawa, a veteran manga editor, walks away from his job at a big publisher after decades in the business. Without quite meaning to, he starts reconnecting with the artists he once worked with, many of whom have struggled. It is thoughtful, melancholy, and beautifully drawn, a great fit for readers curious about how manga is made.
378: Tsubasa: Those With Wings by Natsuki Takaya (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi comedy from the creator of Fruits Basket. In a war-torn future, Kotobuki is a young thief who wants to go straight. She sets out with Raimon, a former soldier, to find the legendary Tsubasa, said to grant any wish, though plenty of others are hunting it too. It is funny, sweet, and adventurous, a fun early work for Takaya fans.
380: Kannagi by Eri Takenashi (Bandai) is a supernatural comedy. High schooler Jin Mikuriya carves a statue from the wood of a sacred tree that was cut down, and to his shock, it comes to life as Nagi, a self-proclaimed goddess who moves in with him. She says she must cleanse the town of impurities, but she also loves TV and snacks. It is silly, sweet, and lively, a good fit for fans of quirky romantic comedies.
384: Crazy Food Truck by Kemuri Karakara (Viz Media) is an action comedy set after the end of the world. Gordon is a gruff ex-soldier who just wants to drive his food truck across the wasteland and cook. Then he finds Arisa, a mysterious girl lying in the road, who insists on joining him and brings trouble everywhere they go. It mixes road trip, cooking, and gunfights, a fun read for fans of post-apocalyptic adventure.
387: Ray by Akihito Yoshitomi (ADV) is a sci-fi medical drama. Ray was raised in an orphanage that secretly harvested children's organs, and after her rescue she was given new eyes that let her see through skin like an x-ray. Now grown, she works as a black-market surgeon, taking on dangerous cases while searching for answers about her past. It is tense and dramatic, a good pick for fans of Black Jack.
391: Until the Full Moon by Sanami Matoh (Broccoli Books) is a fantasy romantic comedy. Marlo is half vampire and half werewolf, and whenever the moon is full, he turns into a girl. His childhood friend David, a vampire, has loved him for years and is thrilled by the arrangement, even if Marlo isn't. It is light, silly, and sweet, a fun read for fans of supernatural romance.
393: Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair, based on the game by Spike Chunsoft (Dark Horse), is a mystery thriller. Hajime Hinata arrives at the elite Hope's Peak Academy, only to wake up on a tropical island with his new classmates. Their teacher, a bear named Monokuma, tells them the only way off is to kill a classmate and get away with it. It is tense, twisty, and darkly funny, best for fans of the games and murder mysteries.
394: Danganronpa Another Episode: Ultra Despair Girls by Hajime Touya (Dark Horse) is an action horror manga based on the game. Komaru Naegi has been locked in an apartment for a year with no idea why, and when she finally escapes, she finds her city overrun by killer Monokuma robots led by a gang of children. She teams up with the writer Toko Fukawa to survive. It is dark, chaotic, and gripping, best for fans of the Danganronpa series.
395: Reborn as a Vending Machine, I Now Wander the Dungeon by Hirukuma (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy light novel. A man who loved vending machines dies and wakes up as one, stuck in a dangerous dungeon, unable to move and able to say only a few phrases. Then a strong, kind girl named Lammis finds him and starts carrying him around. It is goofy, cozy, and surprisingly sweet, a fun pick for fans of offbeat isekai.
